correctness.rationale: For \(s=p+q\), exact algebra gives \(2pq=s(s-\Delta)\), \(r_1=e^s(1-s+\Delta)\), and \(r_2=e^s(1-\Delta/s)\). The zero-mass ratio is strictly below one. The exact feasible bounds \(\Delta\le s\le2\Delta\) follow from \(p^2+q^2\le(p+q)^2\) and \(p^2+q^2\ge(p+q)^2/2\). At fixed \(\Delta\), differentiating proves that \(r_1\) decreases and \(r_2\) increases in \(s\), so the sharp endpoint values and equality cases follow. The \(\log2\) crossover and strict comparison with \(1/(1-\Delta)\) are exact scalar inequalities. The checker is regression only.

value.rationale: The claim resolves the first heterogeneous finite-dimensional case of an explicit open Poisson-binomial density-ratio conjecture and is stronger than merely verifying the conjectured bound: it gives the exact worst-case function at fixed \(\Delta\), all extremizers, and the structural switch at \(\Delta=\log2\).
